children: President Trump said Saturday that Ukraine should halt attacks on Russian oil refineries and called for President Zelenskyy to be replaced, a day after announcing an agreement with Russia's Vladimir Putin to boost diesel exports and a U.S. Treasury Department waiver for sanctioned Russian fuel.

"I think it's time for Ukraine to get a new president... who can make a deal" with Russia, Trump told reporters at the White House, blaming Zelenskyy for Russia's continuing war on the country and Ukraine's attacks on Russian refineries for high diesel prices in the U.S. and worldwide.
Zelenskyy had criticized the U.S. decision to help release Russian diesel fuel into the global markets "a gift to Putin," saying the move will give Russia more resources to continue the war.

The Trump-Zelensky clash marks the lowest point in the two leaders’ relationship since their shouting match in the Oval Office in early 2025 and risks undermining months of European efforts to persuade Trump to maintain U.S. support for Ukraine and pressure on Russia.

For Ukraine, stopping the refinery strikes would mean giving up its main leverage to force Russia to stop the war.
On Saturday, Russian air attacks hit residential buildings in the Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia, reportedly killing at least 20 people.
